correctness.rationale: Cyclic Fourier eigenvalues yield the exact shell mass pairing via irreducible dyadic cyclotomic polynomials. Positive four-support counting proves two distinct shells require all weights equal; equal weights admit at most two shells. Extremal supports and all rational nullity levels are constructed. The irrational polynomial factors into one order-two root and two primitive eighth roots. Exact full support enumerations for N=8,16,32 and symbolic factor checks corroborate, without replacing, the proof.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: A prior result fully covering this claim would need arbitrary positive rational four-tap weights, the at-most-one-shell/equality law, and a real-irrational failure family. The inspected Lam theorem supplies the first divisibility step only; the equal-weight table covers a strictly narrower subfamily. Thus under accessible evidence the full claim is not a restatement of known results, although equivalence in older filter literature is unresolved.

originality.rationale: Classical cyclotomic theorem and known equal-weight four-point shell classification are acknowledged as covered. The distinguishing positivity-plus-rational four-support one-shell rigidity, sharp unequal-weight nullity/equality criterion and real-irrational positive counterfamily are not implied by inspected exact sources or retrieved statements. An unindexed equivalent weighted-filter theorem is possible; novelty is best-knowledge rather than certified.
residual_risks: The full text of record 68cf8ce2dd05 could not be inspected; its public summary is strictly equal-weight, but a weighted corollary may be present.
Some pages of the 2002 4-Circulant Graphs paper were inaccessible.
Unindexed older weighted cyclotomic-filter literature might independently contain the support-four deduction or positive irrational construction.

value.rationale: Provides a sharp and structurally motivated one-shell rigidity theorem, all attainable nonzero nullities, exact extremizer geometry, and a positive irrational infinite-family boundary for sparse cyclic convolution invertibility. It is more than an implementation of the known cyclotomic divisibility lemma.
